host.title: Host
host.description: Hostname or IP address of the Windows host. Kerberos needs the host's DNS name.

transport.title: Transport
transport.description: Protocol that carries the WMI queries. DCOM uses TCP 135 and a dynamic RPC port; WinRM uses HTTPS on TCP 5986.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: Authentication protocol for the Windows account: NTLMv2, or Kerberos for a domain account over DCOM.

username.title: Username
username.description: Windows account that reads WMI on the host, as `DOMAIN\user`, `user@domain` or a local account name. Kerberos needs `user@domain`, with the Active Directory DNS domain.

autodetection_retry.title: Detection retry
autodetection_retry.description: How often to retry the initial connection when the job fails to start, in seconds. Zero disables retries.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Time limit for one collection, including the connection and every enabled query, in seconds.

collectors.title: Metric groups
collectors.description: Metric groups to collect. Each enabled group runs one WMI query per collection, the memory group four, the network group six, and the system, disk and SMB groups two. Keep at least one group enabled.

cpu.title: CPU
cpu.description: Collect processor utilization by mode, in total and per logical processor.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Collect physical and available memory, commit charge, paging activity, page faults, kernel memory pools, the system cache and page lists, the usage of each paging file, and the free and standby memory of each NUMA node.

system.title: System
system.description: Collect the number of processes and threads, context switches, processor queue length, uptime, the host's clock offset and its Remote Desktop sessions.

network.title: Network
network.description: Collect traffic, packets, errors, drops, speed and output queue length per network interface, the host's total traffic, and TCP and UDP packets, connections and errors.

disk.title: Disk
disk.description: Collect available and used space per fixed drive, and bandwidth, operations, latency, utilization and queue per physical disk.

smb.title: SMB
smb.description: Collect the SMB file server's traffic, sessions, logons, open files, logon and access errors and resource shortages, and the open files, requests, connections and traffic of each share.

time.title: Time synchronization
time.description: Collect the Windows Time service's offset from its time source, NTP round-trip delay and number of answering time sources. Needs Windows Server 2016 or later.

tls_ca.title: TLS CA file
tls_ca.description: Path on the poller to the PEM file of the CA that issued the WinRM listener certificate. Leave empty to use the system trust store.

kdc.title: Kerberos KDCs
kdc.description: Domain controllers that issue the Kerberos tickets, as host names or IP addresses with an optional port. Leave empty to find them in DNS.

host.ui:help: The value identifies the job's virtual node, so changing it later creates a new node. With WinRM, it must match a name in the listener certificate.

transport.ui:help:
DCOM needs no extra Windows service: enable the built-in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) firewall rules. The RPC traffic is encrypted.

WinRM needs an HTTPS listener with a certificate the poller trusts. It uses one fixed port, which is easier to allow through firewalls between networks.

auth.ui:help:
NTLMv2 works with local and domain accounts, any host name or IP address, and both transports.

Kerberos needs a domain account, the host's DNS name as Active Directory knows it, the DCOM transport, TCP port 88 from the poller to a domain controller, and clocks within five minutes of the domain's. Choose it where the domain refuses NTLM.

kdc.ui:help:
Each entry is a host name or IP address with an optional port, such as `dc1.example.com` or `dc1.example.com:88`; the port defaults to 88.

When empty, the plugin looks up the `_kerberos._tcp` DNS SRV records that Active Directory publishes for the domain, which needs a DNS server that answers for the domain.

vnode.ui:help: Leave empty and the job creates a virtual node for the Windows host, named after its computer name. To use a virtual node you manage instead, define it in `vnodes.conf` first, then enter its name here.
